newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -Bunds neutral, 100.40 support must hold.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -Bunds neutral, 100.40 support must hold.

text.p: September Bund futures on LIFFE have a neutral chart picture with limited upside but analysts said failure to hold 100.40 would trigger a major decline.
"Bearish sentiment is still there," said Nico Bakker, technical analyst at ABN-AMRO in Amsterdam.
A diamond reversal pattern had been forming since December on June and September contracts, he said. This would be confirmed, with negative price implications, if 100.40 fell.
On the upside, the September contract had initial resistance at 101.55, followed by 101.85, Bakker said.
By 0700 GMT, September Bunds were 0.04 higher at 101.36.
September Bunds lost their upside vigour after touching a contract high of 101.88 on June 17, retreating back to the early June range last week.
Bakker said the diamond formation was in progress on weekly charts, providing solid support and resistance levels for the market.
"If the 100.40 level is taken out on the downside a major decline will follow," said Bakker, adding that first test of support would come at 99.00, followed by 96.00.
On the upside, the diamond formation would be negated if the market survived above 101.85, Bakker said.
At LIFFE, Carol Harmer, a trader and analyst at Kempton's Technical Analysis said a breach of 101.40, would set in place rallies to 101.58, the high on June 19, then to 101.61/64.
"The close at the highs of the day on Friday do suggest that further strength will be evident in today's session," she added.
If however the market balked at 101.40, it could drift back to the 101.25/20 support zone which is the low in mid-June.
A trader from a German bank said 101.58 was unlikely to break. He pegged support at 100.94/95 -- last week's lows. "The market's looking for direction, it's going to be rangebound," he said.
September Euromark futures were quoted 0.01 up at 96.83.
